watercress (WC) colour, chlorophylls, vitamin C content and POD activity were affected by blanching, frozen storage, and storage temperature, but not by freezing.
watercress frozen storage at −30 °C was the best condition for preserving colour and vitamin C contents.

watercress colour, chlorophylls, vitamin C and POD activity changes during freezing and frozen-storage can be successfully described by mathematical equations, which can be useful to predict watercress quality during storage and to design new freezing processes.

the effects of freezing and frozen storage on watercress quality, which could be a useful tool for the frozen storage of this vegetable.
the effects of freezing and frozen storage conditions on the quality parameters of watercress.

the biochemical and colour stability of watercress during freezing and frozen-storage processes, and it provides valuable information to the food industry for the development of new frozen products and the optimization of the frozen-storage conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
watercress frozen storage is not affected by the temperature, but by the blanching process.

the water blanching and freezing processes induced significant changes on watercress quality attributes, but frozen storage at −7 °C was the best option to maintain the nutritional and sensory quality of watercress during the 400 days.
freezing and frozen storage of watercress did not promote significant changes in the nutritional quality and colour of this vegetable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
watercress frozen storage at −15 °C for 200 days is a suitable option for maintaining the nutritional value and colour quality of this vegetable.
freezing did not affect watercress nutritional quality, but frozen storage promoted significant colour and AA degradation, and POD residual activity was reduced during frozen storage.
watercress frozen storage at −7 °C was the best option to maintain the initial quality of the product.
The main takeaway from our work is that
watercress can be frozen for 400 days at −30 °C with a high retention of its quality.
watercress is a good candidate for frozen storage, since its quality parameters were maintained for at least 400 days.
watercress is a suitable vegetable to be processed by freezing, and that water blanching is not necessary for this purpose, which is of great importance in terms of energy and time savings.
